questions.question: Describe how states secure their perceived 'National Interests'. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• States secure national interests through diplomacy and alliances—strengthen military and
  • economic capabilities—use soft power and international institutions to safeguard sovereignty
  • and security.

questions.question: Apply Liberalism to the European Union. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Liberalism in EU -promotes cooperation—emphasizes shared institutions and collective
  • decision-making—supports integration through trade, law, and democratic values.

questions.question: Interpret 'Track I diplomacy'. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Track I diplomacy - involves official negotiations —conducted by state representatives —
  • focuses on formal agreements and conflict resolution at governmental level.

questions.question: Analyse the tension between globalization and state sovereignty. / [CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Globalization enhances interdependence —yet challenges sovereignty through external
  • influence—states struggle to balance autonomy with global economic and political pressures.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write why the Global South is not a monolithic bloc. / [CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Global South is diverse in history and economy —different colonial legacies and political
  • systems—unequal possession of power and resources -varied development trajectories -
  • prevent it from being monolithic bloc.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Associate the "League of Nations" in the 'First great Debate in IR'. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• League of Nations reflected idealist hopes—peace-making-central to First Great Debate in
  • IR—international security and cooperation-idea of global rule of law-criticized for weaknesses
  • but shaped discourse on collective security.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Compare Realist and Liberal views on "Anarchy." / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Realists view anarchy as absence of authority in the international system —absolute
  • lawlessness-leading to conflict and power struggles —anarchy is a permanent condition -
  • pessimistic view-Liberals see it as space for cooperation through institutions -anarchy can be
  • transformed-optimistic view.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain 'brain drain'. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Brain drain refers to skilled migration —talented professionals leave home countries —
  • results in loss of expertise and development challenges -causing loss of talent -reduced
  • innovation- slowing economic and social development in the home country.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain 'International Political Economy'. / [CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• International Political Economy -analyse how political institutions, power relations
  • economic systems interact to shape policy- development outcomes- global inequality- studies
  • interaction of politics and economics—global capitalist system-focuses on trade, finance, and
  • globalization—explains power relations shaping global markets.

questions.question: Describe how interdisciplinary approach can improve policy-making regarding global governance / [CO1, CO2] [5x6 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Interdisciplinary approach integrates economics, politics, sociology —offers holistic
  • solutions for global governance —improves policy -making by addressing complex,
  • interconnected challenges-for example addressing climate change collectively.

questions.question: Discuss the Global Digital Infrastructure / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Global digital infrastructure includes internet backbones, data centres, and cloud
  • networks—enables connectivity across nations —supports e -commerce, governance, and
  • communication- raises concerns of digital divide and cybersecurity.

questions.question: Describe the different stages generally seen in regional integration / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Regional integration begins with preferential trade agreements —progresses to free trade
  • areas and customs unions —later evolves into common markets and political unions -
  • reflecting deeper cooperation.

questions.question: Examine the relevance of Prisoners’ Dilemma in 21st-century international politics. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Prisoners’ Dilemma illustrates mistrust in cooperation —a situation where two
  • individuals/actors acting in self-interest produce a worse outcome for both than cooperation-
  • applies to arms control, climate agreements, and trade—shows how rational self-interest can
  • hinder collective gains in modern international politics.

questions.question: Write how the study of Culture informs IR theory / [CO4, CO5] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Culture informs IR theory by shaping identity and norms—explain how these shape state
  • behaviour, cooperation, and conflict in global politics -explains behaviour beyond material
  • interests—highlights values, traditions and narratives that influence diplomacy, conflict
  • resolution, and global governance.
